problem: Navigation benchmarks and models each handle a single goal modality: PointNav, ObjectNav with 6-21 closed-set categories, ImageNav, or language. They are also episodic, resetting the scene after each goal. No reproducible benchmark tests one agent on open-vocabulary goals given as a category, a language description or an image, with a sequence of goals in the same scene where past experience can be reused.
motivation: Real household robots need goals in several modalities. A category alone ('plate') is often not specific enough, and taking photos of every object is impractical. Such robots also run for long periods in the same home, so they should use memory of objects and areas they have already seen to become more efficient. A concurrent real-world GOAT system (Chang et al.) is closed-set (15 categories) and slow to evaluate, so a simulated, reproducible, open-vocabulary benchmark is needed to study memory, modality and robustness.
key_idea: GOAT-Bench is an open-vocabulary, lifelong navigation benchmark on 181 HM3DSem scenes: each episode chains 5-10 subtasks whose goals are an object category, an auto-generated language description or an instance image. On it the authors compare modular explicit-map agents with end-to-end RL agents that have or lack implicit (GRU) memory.
insight: Explicit memory, not raw recognition, drives efficiency. Dropping the map between subtasks halves Modular GOAT's SPL (17.6→9.4) and cuts SR (26.4→21.2). Dropping the RL monolithic policy's carried-over GRU hidden state barely changes it (SPL 9.4→9.0, SR 16.8→14.9), so the implicit memory is not capturing a usable scene map; qualitatively, the agent re-explores to find objects it has already seen. Goal encoders matter per modality. CLIP embeddings lack instance-specific detail for language and image goals: the LanguageNav skill reaches only 17.1 SR on Val Seen. Cross-view-consistent CroCo-v2 embeddings make the image-goal skill the strongest (48.2 SR) and about 15 points better in SR than Modular GOAT on image goals. The skill chain is also most robust to goal noise (25% average SR drop vs 53% for Modular GOAT), partly because Detic fails on uncommon synonyms.
method: Task: at each step the agent (Stretch embodiment, 1.41 m tall, 17 cm radius) gets 360x640 RGB, depth, GPS+Compass and the current subtask goal. Actions are MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30° and STOP. A subtask succeeds if STOP is called within 1 m of the goal instance within 500 actions, and the scene is not reset between subtasks.

Dataset: 145 train / 36 val HM3DSem scenes; 5k train episodes per scene (725k total) and 10 val episodes per scene. Each episode samples 5-10 subtasks with a uniformly sampled modality, all goals on the start floor, and the first goal 1-30 m from the start. Val splits are Val Seen, Val Seen Synonyms and Val Unseen, separated by category.

Goal sources: category goals come from HM3D-OVON (open vocabulary). OVIIN extends Instance-ImageNav to open vocabulary (7.7k train image goals over 264 categories; 2.9k val over 164). LanguageNav descriptions (5.4k train / 1.9k val) are generated automatically: take the viewpoint with maximum frame coverage, get BLIP-2 attribute captions, add simulator bounding boxes and categories of nearby objects, then prompt GPT-3.5-Turbo.

SenseAct-NN Skill Chain: three separately RL-trained (VER) CNN+GRU skill policies, all on a frozen CLIP-RN50 RGB encoder with 32-d GPS/compass embeddings and a 2-layer 512-d GRU. Goal encoders are a frozen CLIP text encoder for ObjectNav (300M steps), frozen BERT [CLS] for LanguageNav (300M steps), and CroCo-v2 ViT-B with adapters on 112x112 input for OVIIN (200M steps). A planner switches skill by goal modality and resets the hidden state each subtask.

SenseAct-NN Monolithic: a single policy with the same architecture and frozen CLIP image/text goal encoders (1024-d), trained with VER for 500M steps on GOAT train episodes. The GRU hidden state is carried across subtasks as implicit memory.

Evaluated modular baselines: Modular GOAT keeps a semantic plus instance top-down map built from Detic, depth and pose. It matches goals with keypoint matching for images and CLIP cosine similarity for language, filters instances by category, and explores frontiers. CoW matches all goals purely with CLIP. GOAT-GTSem, which uses ground-truth semantics, is an oracle reference.
Metrics: SR and SPL per subtask. The SPL shortest path starts from where the agent ended the previous subtask.

setting.backbone: Frozen CLIP ResNet-50 visual encoder + frozen goal encoders (CLIP text/image; BERT for LanguageNav skill; CroCo-v2 ViT-B with adapters for image skill) + 2-layer 512-d GRU policy trained with RL (VER)
setting.training_data: RL in Habitat on 145 HM3DSem train scenes. Monolithic policy: GOAT train episodes (5k per scene, ~725k episodes), 500M steps. Skill policies: task-specific OVON / LanguageNav / OVIIN training sets for 300M/300M/200M steps. Language goals are auto-generated by BLIP-2 + GPT-3.5-Turbo.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (360x640, resized/center-cropped to 224x224 or 112x112) + GPS+Compass; depth is also available (used by modular baselines)
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30° / LOOK_UP/DOWN 30° / STOP; 500 actions per subtask
setting.privileged: none for the RL policies beyond the task's GPS+Compass sensor. Modular GOAT baseline uses ground-truth pose + depth and category information to filter instances; GOAT-GTSem oracle uses GT semantics.

numbers_note: This is a benchmark paper: every evaluated method is a baseline. Only the two RL agents trained by the authors (Skill Chain, Monolithic) and the OVON skill are listed. The authors' evaluations of Modular GOAT (26.3/17.5, 33.8/24.4, 24.9/17.2 SR/SPL on Val Seen / Val Seen Synonyms / Val Unseen) and CoW are omitted as prior methods; the grey GOAT-GTSem oracle (56.7/40.3, 58.4/43.5, 54.3/41.0) is likewise omitted. The same appendix table also gives the other skill policies on the paper's own per-modality sets (Val Seen / Unseen Easy / Unseen Hard SR/SPL): LanguageNav 17.1/7.8, 16.9/8.1, 13.5/6.1 and OVIIN 48.2/22.3, 45.8/21.6, 45.3/22.3. Its 'Val Unseen Easy/Hard' naming differs from the main 3-split naming, and it is unclear how it maps to HM3D-OVON's final Val Seen Synonyms / Val Unseen. Per-modality, memory-ablation, over-time and noise-robustness results are mainly shown in figures; only some values are quoted in text, e.g. Monolithic without memory SR 14.9 / SPL 9.0 and Modular GOAT without memory 21.2 / 9.4.
results: The SenseAct-NN Skill Chain has the best SR on all three GOAT-Bench splits (29.2 / 38.2 / 29.5 on Val Seen / Seen Synonyms / Unseen) and beats Modular GOAT (26.3 / 33.8 / 24.9). Its SPL is much lower (12.8 / 15.2 / 11.3 vs 17.5 / 24.4 / 17.2), because it keeps no memory across subtasks. The Monolithic RL policy with implicit GRU memory is weakest (16.8 / 18.5 / 12.3 SR). An oracle with ground-truth semantics reaches about 55 SR, so perception is a major bottleneck for modular methods.
limitations: Language goals are generated automatically by BLIP-2 and GPT-3.5 from simulator metadata, with no stated human verification, so descriptions may be noisy or ambiguous. Episodes are single-floor, and only validation splits (no test server) are reported.

All baselines score low in absolute terms. The implicit GRU memory of the end-to-end policy is shown to be largely ineffective, and CLIP goal embeddings fail on instance-specific language and image goals. The benchmark exposes the problem more than it offers a strong solution.
Simulation only. The modular baseline relies on ground-truth pose and depth and on category information for instance filtering.
